commit.message:
docs: fix 61 broken internal links (#729)

* docs: fix 61 broken internal links

Every one of these resolved to the Fern **home page** rather than a 404, which is
why they survived: a reader clicking "goTo" landed somewhere plausible and the
link looked alive. Verified against the deployed site's own sitemap, the
authoritative route list, not re-derived from docs.yml.

Three causes, all in how Fern builds routes:

- **A doubled slug segment.** The route is tab slug + section slug + page slug,
  and a section with no explicit `slug:` still contributes one from its title. So
  the reference pages live at `/reference/reference/<page>`. 18 links used the
  single-segment form, 16 of them to the install CLI page. The ai, contribute and
  support tabs had the same problem.
- **Case and hyphens.** Action routes publish lowercased and unhyphenated, so
  `/docs/actions/goTo`, `/docs/actions/run-shell` and `/docs/actions/stopRecord`
  were all dead. Routing is case-sensitive, confirmed against the live site.
- **Routes that never existed.** `/docs/actions` is a `folder:` entry with no
  landing page, and 9 links pointed at it; they now point at the page that
  actually lists the actions. `/reference/schemas` and `/docs/selectors` are the
  same shape. A few others named pages by an old slug.

One stale anchor too: ci/overview linked `#step-5-fail-ci-when-tests-fail`, but
that heading is Step 6 since a renumber.

The trap is recorded in docs/AGENTS.md, with how to check a route instead of
guessing, since this is exactly the class of error that regrows silently.

No behavior change, so no ADR. Vale clean across all 32 files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: fix the CLI reference link in its generator, not its output

`docs/fern/pages/reference/cli.mdx` is generated, and the workflow that checks it
says so: "Do not hand-edit". My link sweep edited the output, so `cli-ref` failed
the moment it regenerated the page. Both links live in
`docs/.scripts/buildCliReference.js`, so they are fixed there and the page is
regenerated from it. `npm run docs:build-cli-ref` now leaves no diff.

Also addresses the review's point that three labels over-promised once their
target moved to the actions list:

- "its action reference" now says to find the action in "How testing works" and
  open its page, since the per-action page is still where the outputs are.
- "Actions reference" in two link lists now names what the target actually is.
- The "Schemas" label implied an index; it names the config schema instead.

Typed `docs:` rather than `fix:` on purpose. Commit type is the only release
signal, and nothing here changes shipped behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(agents): note that the CLI reference page is generated

Follows the gate I tripped in this PR: editing pages/reference/cli.mdx looks
like it worked, then `cli-ref` regenerates the page and fails on the diff. Says
where the links actually live and how to regenerate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
ci: measure truncation in API records, not emitted paths

The guard counted the paths the query emitted, but a rename emits two paths for
one record, so a rename could mask a record lost to the API's 3000-entry cap:
3000 records including one rename emit 3001 paths, which matches a changed_files
of 3001 exactly and reads as complete. If the omitted record held the only code
change, the matrix skipped and the placeholders reported green.

The query now emits one line per record as `@tsv`, pairing the new path with the
old one. The record count drives the truncation check; the paths are recovered by
splitting on the tab, which keeps both halves of a rename in the selector's input.

Simulated against a stubbed `gh`, with the finding's own scenario first:

  renamemask   2 records for 3 changed files -> truncated   -> code=true
  renameclean  1 record  for 1 changed file  -> complete    -> code=true
  docsonly     2 records for 2 changed files -> complete     -> code=false
  metafail     metadata call fails           -> untrusted    -> code=true

Before this change renamemask produced code=false, which is the bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
